research_period: Milan, Paris and Pitti Uomo menswear shows, June 2026; Premiere Vision Paris, February 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Global: Milan, Paris and Florence runways; premium and mid-market menswear
title: SS27 Men's Material Innovations
summary: Materials for SS27 menswear: crease-proof stretch wool, technical cottons and water-repellent linen, chrome-free leather, softshell and heat-regulating sportswear fabrics.

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
- Herno's travel collection uses crease-proof fabrics, stretch wool and technical materials<sup>[1]</sup>.
- Première Vision highlights technical cottons and water-repellent linens, and compact milanos and softshells<sup>[2]</sup>.
- Margaret Howell's Dr Martens 1461 uses chrome-free leather by C.F. Stead<sup>[1]</sup>.
- Rick Owens used Adidas's Climacool heat-regulation technology<sup>[3]</sup>.
- Balenciaga used lab-grown AMSilk silk in its July 2026 couture<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Readiness
sections.body:
| Material | Readiness (Forecut assessment) |
|---|---|
| Stretch and crease-proof wool | Ready |
| Water-repellent linen, technical cotton | Ready from specialist mills |
| Chrome-free leather | Ready; limited supply |
| Heat-regulating sport fabrics | Ready in sportswear |
| Lab-grown silk | Early; showpieces only |

design_implications: - Use technical wools in travel tailoring; water-repellent linen for unlined outerwear.
commercial_implications: - Verify every sustainability claim before using it.

sources.title: Between heatwave and restraint: menswear trends from Paris
